zh.label: 片刻随记
zh.title: 美女劝我多做颜值视频，但我想先做……
zh.excerpt: 一件事有价值，自己也擅长，并不意味着现在就要投入最多精力。先做自己愿意反复使用、也愿意继续改好的东西。
zh.content:
朋友给了我一个建议。

聊到做工具还是做内容，她说：

> 在做工具和做内容之间，我感觉你是不是更适合去做内容，视觉方面是你的优势。

我理解这份好意。审美和视觉表达，确实是我愿意继续用下去的能力。视频，也是一种值得尝试的表达方式。

但我当时的回复很直接：

> 嗯。我先做满足、取悦自己的工具。
> 
> 做内容，暂时不是取悦我自己。

发完这两句话，我觉得自己的优先级清楚了一点。

一件事有价值，自己也擅长，并不意味着现在就要把最多的精力放在那里。

**先做自己愿意投入的事。**

![先做让自己开心的东西：工具、音乐，与自己的节奏。](/assets/notes/2026-10-05-create-at-your-own-pace/cover.png)

## 01｜“你应该做”，有时候会越来越多

你会设计，就应该多发作品。

你能表达，就应该做视频。

你在做产品，就应该持续更新、展示过程、经营账号。

每一条建议，单独看都挺有道理。放在一起，却像同时打开了十几个窗口，每一个都在提醒你：该我了。

可一天的时间和精力，还是那么多。

如果什么都接下来，最后很容易变成：每件事都在推进，自己却越来越不知道，今天最想做的是哪一件。

所以我想先问自己一个小问题：

**假如今天没有人催，没有数据等着检查，我愿意把这几个小时花在哪里？**

现阶段，我的答案是：先把满足自己需要的工具做好。

## 02｜先做一个自己明天还愿意打开的东西

上一篇，我写了《用 AI 做了几个产品，慢慢拼出了自己想过的生活》。

早上看看世界，上午读一章，中午休息一会儿。这些需要很具体，我也确实会在自己的生活里用到。

当自己每天使用一个工具，就容易遇到那些藏在细节里的问题：这里多点了一次，那里读起来有些费劲，这段声音还不够舒服。

这样的反馈，离我很近。

改完以后，自己能直接感受到变化。明天再打开，它比昨天顺手了一点，这件事就会给我继续做下去的理由。

当然，自己喜欢，并不能自动证明别人需要，更不能自动证明有人愿意付钱。

后面还是要听真实反馈，观察使用，慢慢验证价值。

但至少在起点上，我知道自己为什么想把它做出来。

## 03｜同样是做内容，冥想曲我就愿意先做

有意思的是，我并没有因此把所有内容创作往后放。

我紧接着又回了一句：

> 做冥想曲，是取悦我自己，所以会先做。

音乐当然也是内容。但对我来说，做一段自己想听的冥想曲，动力很直接。

我会期待它完成，也会想把它放进自己的日常里听。再慢慢整理进一休冥想，让有相似需要的人也能听见。

创作本身让我愿意投入，做出来的东西又能回到生活里。

这就够我先动手了。

同样叫“做内容”，有些事情让我想着“该更新了”，有些事情让我想着“还想再试一版”。

我想多留一点时间给后者。

也许过一阵，我会找到一种自己很喜欢的视频表达。到那个时候，再把精力挪过去，也完全来得及。

“暂时”这两个字，本来就给变化留着位置。

![喜欢的创作，也能连接真实的需要：自己愿意做，让人发现，也在生活里用得上。](/assets/notes/2026-10-05-create-at-your-own-pace/create-discover-use.png)

## 04｜豆豆龙和虾子曰，慢慢长出自己的样子

豆豆龙和虾子曰的 IP 与内容，我会继续做。

聊天里，我说的是：“逐步来吧，会做的。”

一个角色能讲什么故事，用什么语气表达，适合怎样的画面，都需要一点点尝试。

我希望它们有自己的趣味和性格，也能承载我关心的事情：看看更大的世界，发现机会，欣赏不同的美，好好生活。

这需要作品积累，也需要我在做的过程中，找到愿意持续的方式。

先有一张自己喜欢的画、一段讲得顺的故事，再试着变成一小段视频。做完，看看自己和读者的反应，再决定下一步。

想到这里，“以后还要做好多内容”的压力，就变成了“下一件想试什么”的期待。

## 05｜内容要有用：让需要的人找到工具

朋友后来还说：“内容会比工具更有价值。”

我能理解这个判断。内容有自己的价值，也能让更多人认识一个创作者。

而我现阶段更想试的，是让两者形成联系。

我在聊天里的原话比较直白：

> 内容，用来做流量，给工具导流。

展开来说，就是用审美、故事、声音和观点，让别人先产生兴趣，再看到这些作品可以怎样进入自己的生活。

比如一段让人愿意听完的冥想音乐，可以自然带出它适合怎样的休息场景；一篇有趣的漫画，也可以让人想继续读下去。

内容让人发现，工具让那份兴趣有地方落下来。

不过，内容本身也要值得看、值得听。每次刚产生一点兴趣，就被催着下载，谁都会累。

我希望读者即使不去使用工具，也能从内容里得到一点愉快、启发或新的视角。真正有需要的人，再顺着入口往前走。

这条路有没有商业价值，最后还得看：来了多少合适的人，他们有没有用起来，为什么留下，又愿意为什么付费。

播放量可以帮人看见你。产品能不能继续被需要，还要靠实际体验来回答。

## 06｜允许自己有顺序，也允许顺序改变

“取悦自己”，在这里有一个很具体的意思：我希望日常投入的大部分时间，能连着真实的兴趣和需要。

做自己喜欢的事，当然也会遇到麻烦，也有枯燥的修改和必须承担的责任。

但当方向是自己认可的，那些不那么有趣的环节，就有了愿意完成的理由。

现阶段，我想先做好自己愿意用的工具，先做自己愿意听的音乐，让豆豆龙和虾子曰的内容慢慢生长。

之后遇到新的机会，有了新的兴致，也可以调整。

我不需要今天就给往后所有的创作方式排好座次。

先把眼前真正想做的事，认真往前推一点。

**一休：照顾好身体与情绪，给精力留一点余量。**

**不二：接纳自己擅长一些事，也暂时不想做一些事。**

**三慢：慢下来，慢慢来，慢慢成为。**

**如水：向内扎根，向外流动；顺应变化，不失本心。**

从自己喜欢的东西出发，慢慢找到有相似需要的人。

让作品长出来，也给自己的生活留出位置。

**#一休不二三慢**

文中提到的作品：

- [一休冥想](https://yixiu.wonderelian.com/)
- [虾子曰 · 昨日世界](https://xiazishuo.com/)
- [虾子曰艺术风格图鉴](https://style-atlas.wonderelian.com/)
- [WonderElian · 沿途所作](https://wonderelian.com/zh/#now)

配图取意于艺术风格图鉴推荐的 **Shojo／少女漫画风格**，借用细腻线条、柔和光影和情绪表达，画成年人的日常创作。聊天原话仅作文字摘录，未展示群友头像和群聊信息。

en.label: Field Notes
en.title: A Friend Told Me to Make More Visually Polished Videos. But First, I Want to...
en.excerpt: Being good at something—and knowing it has value—does not mean it deserves most of your energy right now. Begin with what you still want to use and improve tomorrow.
en.content:
A friend offered me a suggestion.

We were talking about making tools versus making content. She said:

> Between tools and content, I wonder whether content might suit you better. Visual expression is one of your strengths.

I understood the kindness behind it. Aesthetic judgment and visual expression are abilities I want to keep using. Video is also a form worth exploring.

But my reply was direct:

> For now, I want to make the tools that meet my own needs and delight me.
> 
> Making content does not delight me in the same way—at least not yet.

After sending those lines, my priorities felt a little clearer.

Something can be valuable, and I can be good at it, without it deserving most of my energy right now.

**Begin with the work you are willing to invest yourself in.**

![Make what brings you joy first: tools, music, and a rhythm of your own. The original cover contains Chinese text.](/assets/notes/2026-10-05-create-at-your-own-pace/cover.png)

## 01｜The List of Things You “Should” Do Keeps Growing

You know design, so you should post more work.

You can express ideas, so you should make videos.

You are building products, so you should keep publishing updates, show the process, and run your accounts.

Each suggestion sounds reasonable on its own. Put them together, though, and it feels like opening a dozen windows at once—each one reminding you that it is next.

The hours and energy in a day remain the same.

If I accept everything, I can easily end up advancing every task while becoming less certain about which one I actually want to do today.

So I ask myself a small question:

**If nobody were urging me and no metric needed checking, where would I choose to spend the next few hours?**

For now, my answer is to make the tools that meet my own needs.

## 02｜Make Something You Will Still Want to Open Tomorrow

In my previous essay, I wrote about building several products with AI and slowly piecing together the life I want.

I look at the world in the morning, read a chapter before noon, and rest for a while at midday. These needs are specific, and the products are things I genuinely use in my own life.

Using a tool every day reveals the problems hidden in details: an extra tap here, a passage that is harder to read there, a sound that is not yet comfortable enough.

That feedback is close to me.

When I improve something, I can feel the difference directly. I open it again tomorrow, and it works a little better than yesterday. That gives me a reason to continue.

Of course, liking something myself does not prove that other people need it, much less that anyone will pay for it.

The next step still requires listening to real feedback, observing use, and gradually validating value.

But at the starting point, I at least know why I want to make it.

## 03｜Meditation Music Is Content I Do Want to Make Now

Interestingly, this does not mean I am postponing every form of content.

I immediately added another reply:

> Making meditation music delights me, so I will do that first.

Music is content too. But making a meditation track I personally want to hear gives me a very direct source of motivation.

I look forward to finishing it, and I want to bring it into my own daily life. Then I can gradually add it to Yixiu Meditation so that people with similar needs can hear it too.

The act of creating makes me want to invest myself, and the finished work returns to ordinary life.

That is enough reason to begin.

Under the same label of “making content,” some tasks make me think, “I should publish an update.” Others make me think, “I want to try one more version.”

I want to leave more time for the second kind.

Perhaps, after a while, I will discover a way of expressing myself through video that I truly enjoy. I can move more energy there when that happens.

The words “not yet” are there to leave room for change.

![Creative work we love can meet real needs: something we want to make, people can discover, and life has room to use. The original artwork contains Chinese text.](/assets/notes/2026-10-05-create-at-your-own-pace/create-discover-use.png)

## 04｜Let Doudoulong and Xiazi Grow into Their Own Characters

I will keep developing the characters and content of Doudoulong and Xiazi.

In the conversation, I said, “One step at a time. I will make it.”

What stories can a character tell? What voice should it use? What kind of images suit it? Each answer needs small experiments.

I want these characters to have their own humour and personality while carrying the things I care about: looking at a larger world, noticing opportunities, appreciating different forms of beauty, and living well.

That requires a body of work. It also requires me to find a way of working that I can sustain.

Begin with an image I like and a story that feels natural to tell. Then try turning it into a short video. Finish it, notice how I and the readers respond, and decide what comes next.

Seen this way, the pressure of “so much content I must make later” becomes curiosity about “what would I like to try next?”

## 05｜Content Should Help the Right People Find the Tool

My friend later said, “Content can be more valuable than tools.”

I understand that view. Content has value of its own, and it can help more people discover a creator.

At this stage, however, I am more interested in connecting the two.

My original reply was blunt:

> Content brings attention and guides people toward the tools.

Put more fully, aesthetics, stories, sound, and ideas can create interest first. Then people can see how a work might enter their lives.

A meditation track someone wants to hear until the end can naturally reveal the kind of rest it supports. An entertaining comic can invite someone to keep reading.

Content creates discovery. A tool gives that interest somewhere to land.

But the content itself still has to be worth seeing or hearing. Anyone gets tired when every spark of interest is immediately answered with a demand to download something.

Even if a reader never uses the tool, I hope the content gives them some pleasure, insight, or a new perspective. People with a real need can follow the path further.

Whether this has commercial value ultimately depends on practical questions: how many suitable people arrive, whether they use the product, why they remain, and what they are willing to pay for.

View counts can help people notice you. Whether a product continues to matter can only be answered by the experience itself.

## 06｜Give Yourself an Order—and Permission to Change It

Here, “delighting myself” has a concrete meaning: I want most of the time I invest each day to remain connected to genuine interests and needs.

Work we love still brings trouble. It still contains tedious revisions and responsibilities we must carry.

But when the direction is one we believe in, the less interesting parts have a reason to be completed.

For now, I want to improve the tools I am willing to use, make music I want to hear, and let the content of Doudoulong and Xiazi grow gradually.

When new opportunities or new enthusiasm appear, the order can change.

I do not need to rank every form of creation for the rest of my life today.

I only need to move the thing I truly want to do now a little further forward.

**Yixiu—care for the body and emotions, and leave a little space for energy to return.**

**Buer—accept that I am good at some things and do not want to do some others, at least for now.**

**Sanman—slow down, go gradually, and become over time.**

**Like water—take root within and flow outward; adapt to change without losing what matters.**

Begin with what you love, then gradually find people who carry a similar need.

Let the work grow—and leave room for your own life as it does.

**#RestWholenessSlowness**

Works mentioned in this essay:

- [Yixiu Meditation](https://yixiu.wonderelian.com/?lang=en)
- [Xiazi · Yesterday’s World](https://xiazishuo.com/)
- [Xiazi Style Atlas](https://style-atlas.wonderelian.com/)
- [WonderElian · Along the Way](https://wonderelian.com/en/#now)

The illustrations draw on the **Shojo manga style** recommended by Style Atlas, using delicate lines, soft light, and emotional expression to portray adult creative life. The conversation is represented only through short text excerpts; no participant portraits or group-chat information are shown.
